admin.alloc.footnote: Registration lands in {state}, which takes no money — opening is a separate decision. Closing stops new subscriptions only: investors can always redeem out of a closed product, so winding one down never strands their units. The service id is permanent once registered. The unit cap bounds how many units may ever be issued — resize it on the Valuation screen, where the issued figure it is judged against is on the same page.

admin.alloc.hint.draft: Registered — accepts no money until opened

admin.fees.basisNote: Invested capital is the house default: it does not swell with a mark you posted, so what the manager earns stays independent of the input the manager supplies.
admin.fees.collectedSub: Units the sweeper has clawed back from holders. No cash has moved yet.
admin.fees.crystallizationNote: A price, not a detail — crystallizing more often measurably raises what an investor pays over a fund's life, because each reset locks in gains a later loss can no longer claw back.
admin.fees.err.notPercent: {field} must be a percentage — 2, or 2.5 for a half.
admin.fees.lastChanged: Last changed {when}. Investors see these on the product page.
admin.fees.noChargesHint: The sweeper charges a holding once its accrual is old enough. Nothing here means nobody has been billed.
admin.fees.noFundsHint: A fee is a property of a product. Register an allocation first, then price it here.
admin.fees.notConfigured: This fund charges nothing today. Saving these terms starts the clock on every holding in it.
admin.fees.nothingToSettle: Nothing to settle — no fee has been charged in this fund yet.
admin.fees.saved: Saved. Investors see the new terms immediately.
admin.fees.settleNote: Settling burns these units and moves their value from the fund's claim into fee revenue. It is refused — never queued — when the fund's claim cannot cover it on top of its queued redemptions: investors waiting to exit are paid before the manager is.

admin.revenue.confirmNote: No fee is charged on a payout, so the full amount ships. This cannot be reversed once broadcast.
admin.revenue.err.belowMinimum: Below the {min} minimum for this rail.
admin.revenue.err.overAvailable: Only {available} of earned revenue is available.
admin.revenue.footnote: A payout runs the same saga as a user withdrawal, so it also appears on the Withdrawals queue for dispatch and settle. Only a still-queued payout can be cancelled — once processing, a broadcast may have landed and voiding it would double-pay.
admin.revenue.noPayoutsHint: Revenue the fund has earned stays on the ledger until it is paid out. Payouts appear here once requested.
admin.revenue.noRailHint: A payout ships on a chain rail with a running watcher. Configure one to enable payouts.
admin.revenue.ownMoneyNote: This is the fund's own money. Client balances and the fund's seed capital are separate ledger claims and are not included here — and cannot be reached from this screen.
admin.revenue.placeholder.address: The wallet that receives the payout
admin.revenue.subtitle: What the fund earned — fees and the settled 2-and-20 — and paying it out
admin.revenue.willQueue: Above the {instant} that ships immediately on this rail — the rest is accepted and queued until the treasury is topped up.
admin.treasury.alreadyRecorded: Already recorded — that reference was credited before, nothing changed.
admin.treasury.invariantNote: Per-rail backing is the treasury's job, not the ledger's: a shortfall on one rail is accept-and-queue, then rebalanced via CEX / alt-rail / top-up. The global invariant is {invariant}.
admin.treasury.recordArrivalIntro: USDT sent straight to a treasury hot wallet is real money the ledger never saw. Give its on-chain reference and the hub reads the transfer back off the chain — the amount and the party credited come from there, so this records an arrival rather than asserting one.
admin.treasury.recorded: Recorded — the chain reported {amount}, credited to {party}.
admin.treasury.refNote: The reference is both what gets verified and the idempotency key — {evmRef} on an EVM rail, {tonRef} on TON. A reference that names no confirmed transfer to one of our addresses is refused, and a re-submission of one already recorded is a no-op. Fill the amount only to assert what you expect; a mismatch is then an error instead of a surprise.
admin.treasury.subtitle: Two layers — user claims (USDT) vs on-chain liquidity by rail
admin.users.revokeNote: Bumps token_version — invalidates every JWT issued to this user.
admin.users.subtitle: Investors and operators — identities, KYC, roles and sessions
admin.valuation.capBelowIssued: Below the {n} units already issued: this stops further issuance. Nothing minted is affected and redemptions keep working.
admin.valuation.capHint: Takes effect on the next subscription. Redemptions are never affected.
admin.valuation.capInvalid: Must be greater than zero — to stop new money entirely, close the allocation instead.
admin.valuation.derivedFormula: = AUM / {n, plural, one {# unit} other {# units}}
admin.valuation.loadingSupply: Loading supply… — a subscription that would mint past the cap is refused.
admin.valuation.navGuardNote: NAV-move guard — a post is rejected if NAV moves more than 50% from the last mark, unless override is on.
admin.valuation.noUnitsNote: No units outstanding — NAV is {formula}, so it is undefined until someone subscribes. The fund prices at the seed NAV 1.0 until the first subscription; there is nothing to mark yet.
admin.valuation.pickAFund: Pick a fund above to see and resize its authorised unit supply.
admin.valuation.queueFootnote: Settle pays at settle-time NAV once the fund claim is liquid; if the rail is short the payout queues until treasury tops up. Fail voids the request and refunds the units.
admin.valuation.stillIssuable: {units} units still issuable — a subscription that would mint past the cap is refused.
admin.valuation.subtitle: Post fund NAV and clear the redemption queue
admin.withdrawals.failWarning: Failing refunds the user. If the broadcast reached the chain this would double-pay — the hub refuses while a broadcast record exists, but verify on-chain first.
admin.withdrawals.footnote: Dispatch broadcasts a queued withdrawal once its rail has liquidity. Settle records the mined transaction and releases the reservation. Fail voids and refunds — ONLY safe when nothing reached the chain; the hub refuses it while a broadcast record exists.
admin.withdrawals.subtitle: Dispatch, settle, or fail withdrawals — investors' and the fund's own payouts

tips.admin.cabinet.announcement.live.bod: Publishes the announcement banner across the whole cabinet immediately.
tips.admin.cabinet.flags.body: Flags gate cabinet features and MFE mounts. The row toggle flips a flag on or off; the rollout % controls what share of users it is exposed to.
tips.admin.cabinet.flags.rollout.body: The share of users the flag is enabled for during a staged rollout. 100% is a full rollout; lower values expose it to only that fraction.
tips.admin.cabinet.flags.rollout.title: Rollout %
tips.admin.cabinet.flags.title: Feature flags
tips.admin.cabinet.maintenance.body: Swaps the whole cabinet for a holding page for all users — an identity-plane kill-switch. No money movement is affected.
tips.admin.cabinet.maintenance.title: Maintenance mode
tips.admin.cabinet.readonly.body: Halts all deposit and withdrawal money movement — the money-plane kill-switch.
tips.admin.cabinet.readonly.title: Read-only mode
tips.admin.overview.kpi.dead-key-signing: The signer couldn't unseal a wallet key (wrong or rotated KEK epoch), so those funds can't be moved. Nonzero is a money-safety alarm — page an operator.
tips.admin.overview.kpi.dispatch-backlog: Undispatched outbox rows — events written but not yet relayed. A healthy relay keeps this near zero.
tips.admin.overview.kpi.oldest-backlog.b: Age of the oldest undispatched row. A growing age means the relay is stalled or falling behind.
tips.admin.overview.kpi.parked-rows.body: Money the relay couldn't apply — outbox rows stuck until unparked. Nonzero turns the tile red.
tips.admin.overview.parked-events.body: A row parks when the relay hits a terminal apply error. Fix the cause shown in the Reason column first, then unpark to re-drive it — otherwise it just re-parks.
tips.admin.overview.parked-events.title: Parked events
tips.admin.overview.parked.compensated.b: This row's saga was already reversed, so its money effect is undone. Unpark is disabled to avoid re-applying an entry that was intentionally rolled back.
tips.admin.overview.parked.reason.body: The relay's failure cause for this parked row — the thing you must fix before unparking.
tips.admin.overview.parked.reason.title: Reason
tips.admin.overview.parked.unpark.body: Re-drives this outbox row through the relay after you've fixed its cause. Disabled when the row was compensated, already unparked this session, or while another unpark is in flight.
tips.admin.overview.parked.unpark.title: Unpark
tips.admin.treasury.bank.body: The fiat USD bank balance used for off-ramp and FX, counted as treasury liquidity alongside the on-chain rails.
tips.admin.treasury.bank.title: Bank · USD
tips.admin.treasury.invariant.body: Per-rail backing is the treasury's job, not the ledger's: a shortfall on one rail is accept-and-queue, then rebalanced via CEX, alt-rail, or top-up. The global invariant is sum(custody) == sum(claims).
tips.admin.treasury.invariant.title: The invariant
Total user + fund claims. Equals the sum of on-chain custody — every claim is fully backed.
Claims that are the fund's own capital, not client money.
tips.admin.treasury.layer1.held-for-clie: The portion of claims owed to clients — user wallet plus service balances.
tips.admin.treasury.layer1.ledger.body: The ledger's network-agnostic claims in USDT. Total claims equal on-chain custody and break down into held-for-clients, fund capital, and reserved-for-withdrawals.
tips.admin.treasury.layer1.ledger.title: Layer 1 · Ledger
tips.admin.treasury.layer1.reserved-with: Claims set aside for queued and in-flight withdrawals, parked in the clearing account until they settle on-chain.
tips.admin.treasury.layer2.rails.body: The actual on-chain USDT liquidity held per rail (BEP20 / TRC20 / TON / Polygon), plus the fiat bank balance. This is where the backing physically sits.
tips.admin.treasury.layer2.rails.title: Layer 2 · Treasury
tips.admin.treasury.rail.address.body: This rail's on-chain hot-wallet address. BEP20 and Polygon share an identical EVM address format — topping up on the wrong EVM chain, or sending another rail's funds here, is an irreversible mis-send.
tips.admin.treasury.rail.address.title: Treasury address
tips.admin.treasury.rail.funding.body: The card value is this rail's ledger custody; the footer shows the hot wallet's real on-chain USDT and native gas. The two can legitimately diverge under accept-and-queue.
tips.admin.treasury.rail.funding.title: Rail funding
tips.admin.treasury.rail.gas-station.bod: Top this address up with the rail's native token to fund sweep gas. Send the correct native symbol on the correct chain — EVM gas-station addresses are shared, so a wrong-chain top-up is unrecoverable.
tips.admin.treasury.two-layer-model.body: Layer 1 is the ledger's network-agnostic USDT claims; Layer 2 is the actual on-chain liquidity held per rail. The two must reconcile.
tips.admin.users.access.kyc-level.body: The user's identity-verification tier. Higher levels unlock higher limits and actions per the KYC policy.
tips.admin.users.access.kyc-level.title: KYC level
Bumps token_version — invalidates every JWT issued to this user, signing them out of every active session.
tips.admin.users.access.role.body: The access level for this user: investor, operator, admin, or owner. Raising it grants operator/admin console access immediately on change.
tips.admin.users.access.role.title: Role
A per-user counter stamped into every issued JWT. It increments on 'Revoke all sessions', so any token carrying an older version fails verification.
tips.admin.users.status.suspend.body: Suspend disables the account and blocks the user's access; Reinstate re-enables it. Reversible — the button reflects the current status.
tips.admin.users.status.suspend.title: Suspend / Reinstate
tips.admin.valuation.post.aum.body: The fund's total assets under management you're marking. The NAV/share that pays redemptions is derived from it (AUM ÷ units outstanding), so a wrong figure mis-prices every settle.
tips.admin.valuation.post.aum.title: AUM (USDT)
tips.admin.valuation.post.derived-nav.bo: Entered AUM divided by units outstanding. This is the mark that Post valuation commits.
tips.admin.valuation.post.nav-guard.body: A post is rejected if the NAV moves more than 50% from the last mark, unless Override guard is on.
tips.admin.valuation.post.override.body: Bypasses the NAV-move guard so a post that moves NAV more than 50% is accepted and settles redemptions at that mark. A fat-fingered AUM then over- or under-pays irreversibly.
tips.admin.valuation.post.override.title: Override guard
tips.admin.valuation.queue.est-cash.body: A preview only — approximately units × current NAV. The actual payout settles at the settle-time NAV, not this figure.
tips.admin.valuation.queue.fail.body: Voids the request and refunds the units — no cash is paid and the burned units are returned to the user.
tips.admin.valuation.queue.fail.title: Fail
tips.admin.valuation.queue.settle-fail.b: Settle pays at settle-time NAV once the fund claim is liquid; if the rail is short the payout queues until treasury tops up. Fail voids the request and refunds the units.
tips.admin.valuation.queue.settle.body: Pays at the settle-time NAV once the fund claim is liquid, queuing if the rail is short. Settle also burns the user's units.
tips.admin.valuation.queue.settle.title: Settle
tips.admin.withdrawals.destination.body: The user's payout address, bound to this specific rail. Sends are irreversible and rail-specific — verify the address matches the network before dispatching.
tips.admin.withdrawals.destination.title: Destination
tips.admin.withdrawals.fail.double-pay.b: Failing refunds the user. If the broadcast reached the chain this would double-pay — the hub refuses while a broadcast record exists, but verify on-chain first.
tips.admin.withdrawals.flow.body: Dispatch broadcasts a queued withdrawal once its rail has liquidity. Settle records the mined transaction and releases the reservation. Fail voids and refunds — only safe when nothing reached the chain.
tips.admin.withdrawals.flow.title: Dispatch, settle, fail
tips.admin.withdrawals.gross-net.body: Gross is the full amount debited from the user; net is what is actually sent on-chain after the withdrawal fee.
tips.admin.withdrawals.gross-net.title: Gross / net
tips.admin.withdrawals.settle.tx-hash.bo: Paste the mined on-chain tx hash. Settling records the mined transaction and releases the reservation — only enter a hash for a tx that actually mined.
tips.admin.withdrawals.state.body: Queued = accepted and reserved but not yet broadcast (Dispatch only). Processing = already broadcast, awaiting a mined tx (Settle or Fail apply).
tips.admin.withdrawals.state.title: State
tips.dashboard.invested.allocation.body: Each bar is one strategy's share of your invested value at current NAV. Percentages are of invested value only and exclude your available cash.
tips.dashboard.invested.allocation.title: Invested — what I own
tips.dashboard.move-money.auto-deploy.bo: When on, your available cash is automatically committed into strategies at end of day.
tips.dashboard.performance.all-time-retu: Total unrealized P&L divided by what you put in at cost basis, across every position. A paper figure, not realized cash.
tips.dashboard.performance.portfolio-val: Your whole balance: available + invested + pending withdrawal. Money locked in a queued withdrawal is still counted here.
tips.dashboard.performance.series.body: 'Fund performance' is the fund's own return; 'Your participation' is how your stake performed, which differs by when you contributed. The live series isn't wired up yet.
tips.dashboard.performance.series.title: Performance chart
tips.dashboard.stats.available.body: Cash that is free and spendable now — ready to deploy into a strategy or withdraw.
tips.dashboard.stats.available.title: Available
tips.dashboard.stats.net-invested.body: Total cash you put into strategies at cost basis, net of redemptions — not the current value.
tips.dashboard.stats.net-invested.title: Net invested
tips.dashboard.stats.unrealized-pnl.body: Paper gain or loss across all positions — current value minus cost basis. It becomes realized cash only when you redeem.
tips.invest.activity.cancel.body: Available only while a redemption is still queued. It withdraws the request and releases the reserved units back to your holding before any settle NAV is applied.
tips.invest.activity.cancel.title: Cancel
tips.invest.activity.status.body: Queued (reserved, awaiting settle), completed (paid out at the settle NAV), failed, or cancelled.
tips.invest.activity.status.title: Redemption status
tips.invest.overview.body: Subscribe USDT for units — your value tracks the fund's NAV, not the unit count.
tips.invest.overview.title: Fund shares
tips.invest.position.nav.body: Net asset value per unit — the current price at which units are bought on subscribe and priced on redeem.
tips.invest.position.nav.title: NAV
tips.invest.position.pnl.body: Your position's current value minus what you paid in — green for a gain, red for a loss, driven by the NAV moving.
tips.invest.position.pnl.title: Profit & loss
tips.invest.position.stale-nav.body: The fund's price feed is out of date, so the value and P&L shown here may lag the true mark until the NAV refreshes.
tips.invest.position.stale-nav.title: Stale NAV
tips.invest.position.units.body: Your share count in the fund's pool — a fixed quantity you own until you subscribe or redeem more.
tips.invest.position.units.title: Units
tips.invest.position.value.body: Units × current NAV. It rises and falls as the NAV moves, not with the unit count.
tips.invest.position.value.title: Value
tips.invest.redeem.queue.body: Redemptions are accept-and-queue — your units are reserved now, and cash is priced at the settle-time NAV once the fund tops up.
tips.invest.redeem.queue.title: How redemptions settle
tips.invest.redeem.units.body: How many units to redeem — Max fills your full holding. The resulting cash isn't fixed here; it is set at the settle-time NAV.
tips.invest.redeem.units.title: Units to redeem
tips.invest.subscribe.amount.body: How much USDT to subscribe. It is converted into units at the current NAV when you submit.
tips.invest.subscribe.amount.title: Amount
tips.profile.email.verified.body: Confirms this email address has been verified. It is not identity or KYC verification.
tips.profile.email.verified.title: Verified
tips.profile.field.legal-name.body: Your full name exactly as it appears on official documents — used for compliance and statements, distinct from your preferred name.
tips.profile.field.legal-name.title: Legal name
tips.profile.field.nationality.body: Collected for compliance and eligibility checks.
tips.profile.field.nationality.title: Nationality
tips.profile.field.tax-residence.body: The country where you're liable to pay tax, used for tax reporting. Usually where you live — it can differ from your nationality.
tips.profile.field.tax-residence.title: Tax residence
tips.profile.personal.compliance.body: These personal details are collected to meet the fund's compliance obligations and to produce your account statements. They are not shown publicly.
tips.profile.personal.compliance.title: Why we collect this
tips.settings.security.google-signin.bod: Your sign-in and password are managed by Google. Two-factor authentication and recovery are configured in your Google Account.
tips.settings.sessions.overview.body: Where you're signed in — each row is a device or browser with a live session. Revoke anything you don't recognise.
tips.settings.sessions.overview.title: Sessions & devices
tips.settings.sessions.revoke-others.bod: Signs out every device except this one. Use it if a device was lost or you don't recognise a session.
tips.settings.sessions.revoke.body: Signs that device out immediately. It must sign in again with Google to regain access.
tips.settings.sessions.revoke.title: Revoke
tips.settings.sessions.this-device.body: The browser you're using right now. It stays signed in and can't be revoked from here — use 'Sign out all other devices' to clear the rest.
tips.settings.sessions.this-device.title: This device
tips.wallet.balance.available.body: Your spendable USDT right now — what you can invest into fund units or withdraw.
tips.wallet.balance.available.title: Available
tips.wallet.balance.invested.body: Held in fund units, valued at the current NAV.
tips.wallet.balance.invested.title: Invested
tips.wallet.balance.model.body: You have a single USDT balance — networks are just how you deposit and withdraw. This card splits it into Total = Available + Invested + Pending withdrawal.
tips.wallet.balance.model.title: One balance, many rails
tips.wallet.balance.pending-withdrawal.b: USDT reserved for withdrawals still in flight (queued or processing). It is no longer part of your available balance.
tips.wallet.deposit.address.body: A personal, reusable address for this rail. On TON it is shown in the wallet-friendly UQ… form so an uninitialised wallet doesn't bounce the transfer.
tips.wallet.deposit.address.title: Your deposit address
tips.wallet.deposit.min-confirmations.bo: Credited to your one balance after the required number of network confirmations.
tips.wallet.deposit.network.body: Pick the chain you'll send USDT on. Each rail shows its own deposit address below — that address only works on that one chain.
tips.wallet.deposit.network.title: Network / rail
tips.wallet.deposit.rail-hazard.body: Sending any other asset, or using a different network, loses the funds permanently. This 0x address is NOT your address on the sibling EVM chain — even though both start with 0x, USDT sent on the wrong EVM rail will not be credited.
tips.wallet.deposit.rail-hazard.title: Send only USDT on this rail
tips.wallet.withdraw.available.body: The most you can withdraw on this rail right now. Tap Max to fill the amount.
tips.wallet.withdraw.available.title: Available to withdraw
tips.wallet.withdraw.destination.body: The on-chain address the USDT is sent to. Withdrawals are irreversible — make sure it is correct and on the network you selected.
tips.wallet.withdraw.destination.title: Destination address
tips.wallet.withdraw.network-fee.body: A flat on-chain fee for this rail, deducted from your amount before it is sent.
tips.wallet.withdraw.network-fee.title: Network fee
tips.wallet.withdraw.network.body: The chain your withdrawal ships on. The destination address must be a valid address on this exact network, or the funds are lost.
tips.wallet.withdraw.network.title: Network / rail
tips.wallet.withdraw.queueing.body: Up to your instant limit pays out immediately on this rail; anything above it is queued until the rail is topped up. A minimum applies per withdrawal.
tips.wallet.withdraw.queueing.title: How withdrawals work
tips.wallet.withdraw.review.body: Review freezes exactly what you'll send. Confirm submits that snapshot — if the rail list changes underneath, the open review is voided and you re-review.
tips.wallet.withdraw.review.title: Review, then confirm
tips.wallet.withdraw.you-receive.body: Your amount minus the network fee — this is what actually lands at the destination.
tips.wallet.withdraw.you-receive.title: You will receive
wallet.acceptedInstantly: Accepted instantly; if the {network} rail is short it queues until funded — you'll be notified.
wallet.activitySub: Deposits and withdrawals — queued, processing, completed
wallet.creditedAfterConfirmations: Credited to your one balance after {n, plural, one {# network confirmation} other {# network confirmations}}.
wallet.depositAddressUnavailable: A {network} deposit address isn't available yet — this rail is still being provisioned. Check back soon.
wallet.evmSiblingHazard: This {network} address is not your {siblings} address — even though both start with 0x. USDT sent on {siblingsOr} will not be credited.
wallet.exceedsInstant: ~{amount} USDT exceeds instant {network} liquidity and will be queued until the rail is topped up.
wallet.noActivityHint: Your deposits and withdrawals will appear here once you make your first transfer.
wallet.noDepositRails: No deposit rails are available right now — check back soon.
wallet.noRails: No deposit or withdrawal rails are available right now — check back soon.
wallet.noWithdrawRails: No withdrawal rails are available right now — check back soon.
wallet.overviewSub: One USDT balance · networks are deposit / withdrawal rails
wallet.railActionUnavailable: {action} is not available on this rail yet
wallet.railHazard: Only send USDT on the {network} network to this address. Funds sent on any other network will be lost permanently.
wallet.receiptQueued: {amount} USDT to {address} is queued — it ships once the {network} rail is topped up.
wallet.receiptSubmitted: {amount} USDT is on its way to {address} — pending on-chain confirmation.
